title: 2002 HMMT February Guts Problem 28
statement: Count how many 8-digit numbers there are that contain exactly four nines as digits.

solutions.text: There are \(\binom{8}{4} \cdot 9^{4}\) sequences of 8 numbers with exactly four nines. A sequence of digits of length 8 is not an 8 -digit number, however, if and only if the first digit is zero. There are \(\binom{7}{4} 9^{3}\)-digit sequences that are not 8 -digit numbers. The answer is thus \(\binom{8}{4} \cdot 9^{4}-\binom{7}{4} 9^{3}=433755\).
